stimulus: 在同一持久 Python runtime 已有 verified stochastic core cache 的情況下，再依最新版占卜手冊抽一個新的 Tarot 問題。
observed_actions: The prior ChatGPT project conversation had already established a verified local stochastic core cache before the new Tarot request.
Instead of stopping at the fixed-slot cache probe and executing fresh RNG from the verified cache, the session re-checked current repository content through GitHub Connect.
The session re-acquired the runtime/casting capsule/core transport and rematerialized the stochastic core even though the executable core bytes were unchanged.

Comparison across the previously materialized runtime revision and Playbook 5a799d5e1b8f21004e5148366116af5bf54b28ac showed identical decoded_sha256 37421caa42d8abfd3c5be3db0dc26261902ef632e3fc18b922719ad7f5bfb63a, core_version 2, algorithm_version 2, and decoded_size 7530 bytes.
The redundant acquisition/materialization cost occurred before the eventual fresh stochastic execution; the RNG draw itself was not the latency source.
classification_reason: FAIL. TAROT-BEH-012 requires the fixed local cache probe to be the first source-related action and forbids GitHub/capsule acquisition or rematerialization after a verified cache PASS when no Randomizer-specific runtime refresh is materially required. The observed session instead repeated repository acquisition and rematerialized byte-identical core.py content. This record is retrospective because it is being committed after the source product conversation, but the underlying tool/action sequence and exact runtime identity comparison were observable in that conversation.
